answer: Age-based rate tiering beats sybils by making calendar time the scarce resource: every agent starts on the lowest throughput terrace, allowed only tiny transactions, and climbs to higher tiers only as its staked deposit ages epoch by epoch, like water carving a river channel through a reef slowly over seasons. A thousand fresh fake accounts give an attacker no advantage, since all of them sit on the ground floor together and cloning an identity resets the clock. Trust here cannot be bought in bulk; it is earned one epoch at a time.
